about: The priest says the first part of the blessing at the altar, then turns to the people and makes the sign of the cross over them. He makes one sign even at a solemn Mass. The threefold blessing belongs to a Pontifical Mass. The blessing is omitted after Benedicámus Dómino and in Masses for the Dead.

about_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
about_citations.locator: Ritus servandus in celebratione Missae, XII, 1–4

s01.narrative: Then the priest kisses the altar, raises his eyes, extends, lifts and joins his hands, bows his head to the Cross, and says:

narrative_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
narrative_citations.locator: Ordo Missae, rubric before Benedicat vos

s03.narrative: Turning towards the people, the priest blesses them once and continues:

narrative_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
narrative_citations.locator: Ordo Missae, rubric for the final blessing

s04.translation: the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

s05.narrative: In Masses for the Dead no blessing is given. After Requiéscant in pace the priest says Pláceat tibi, sancta Trínitas, kisses the altar, and reads the Gospel of Saint John.

w001.function: Subjunctive of wish. “Deus” (w004) is the subject and “vos” (w002) the direct object.

w003.function: Agrees with “Deus” (w004), although it stands before it.

w005.function: Nominative in apposition to “Deus” (w004), not vocative.

w009.function: Nominative singular in apposition to “Deus” (w004), alongside “Pater” (w005) and “Fílius” (w007).
